1000622.etyen:
Internationalism, ultimately from Lithuanian Lietuva (“Lithuania”). The Norwegian form belongs to a Germanic name family represented by German, Danish and Swedish Litauen. Medieval German sources used forms such as Lettowen, reflecting the Lithuanian stem liet-, while the later German form Litauen reflects the Slavic variant with lit-.
The Lithuanian name is first attested in the Latin form Litua in 1009. Its deeper origin is disputed. One influential proposal derives it from the river name Lietava or Lietauka, but several other explanations have also been proposed.

Borrowed from Danish Boel, a younger form of Old Danish Boeld, from Old Norse Bóthildr, a female given name formed from bót (“remedy, help, improvement”) and hildr (“battle, fight”). 1004462.etyen:
1000 (“one thousand”) + meter (“metre”) + stafett (“relay”), literally “1000-metre relay”.
The element meter is from French mètre (“metre”), ultimately from Ancient Greek μέτρον (métron, “measure”), from Proto-Indo-European *meh₁- (“to measure”). Stafett is from older German Stafette (“relay; courier”), from Italian staffetta (“courier; relay race”), originally a derivative of staffa (“stirrup”).
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk 1000 meter stafett and Danish 1000 meter stafet (“Swedish relay”).
